title: Time constructibility of the quasi-polynomial budget
statement: Define $T(n)=2^{(\log_2 n)^2+1}$, where the exponent uses the integer logarithm $\log_2 n=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (in particular, $\log_2 0=0$). Then $T$ is time constructible: for every $n$, $n\le T(n)$, and there are a positive integer $c$ and a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet that, on every binary input $x$, outputs the binary representation of $T(|x|)$ within $c(T(|x|)+1)$ steps.
